Requirement R04 (input): Stop Using Autopilot. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to disengage the autopilot and resume manual control..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-04.1, F-04.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-04.<F>.1, Be-04.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-04.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Allow the pilot to disengage the autopilot and resume manual control.

**Function candidates:**

**F-04.1 — Relinquish automation authority to the pilot.**
The function is to transfer control authority from the autopilot back to the human, i.e. terminate automated flight-path management so the pilot's manual inputs govern the aircraft. Teleology: restore human command authority on demand.

**F-04.2 — Provide a deliberate, error-resistant automation-off action.**
The function is to make disengagement a positive, unambiguous act that resists accidental triggering in a high-vibration/high-workload cockpit — the artefact exists to ensure the pilot only leaves automation when they mean to.

**F-04.3 — Assure the pilot of the post-disengagement control state.**
The function is to close the loop on what the aircraft is now doing (manual vs. still-automated), so the pilot has correct awareness of who holds authority after the action. Teleology: prevent mode confusion at the automation→manual boundary.

---

Note on distinctness and reuse:
- F-04.1 is the core "return control" goal (maps directly to UC 1.4).
- F-04.2 is a safety/integrity goal — could be argued as a Behaviour trait rather than a Function; I include it because "resist unintended disengagement" is a genuine teleological driver in this cockpit, not just a reworded off-switch.
- F-04.3 is a distinct awareness goal and is a strong reuse candidate — it's essentially the same "confirm resulting state" teleology behind R02 (capture-complete confirmation). If we close on F-04.3, its Behaviour/Structure should likely reuse R02's multi-channel alert rather than being built fresh.

Which function do you want to close on?
This is pretty much the same as R03, just in reverse. No need for a lot here.

Agreed. R03 was arm→engage; R04 is its inverse — disengage→manual. Same teleology, opposite direction.

**F-04.1 — Relinquish automation authority to the pilot.** Disengage the autopilot and return manual control on a deliberate command.

The F-04.2 (error-resistance) and F-04.3 (state awareness) concerns don't need separate Functions — they fold in as Behaviour traits, exactly as the press-and-confirm and state-persistence did in R03.

**Closing Function: F-04.1 — Relinquish automation authority to the pilot.**

Moving to Behaviour.
Behaviour is pretty much the same, no?

Yes — mirror of R03's dual-input press-and-confirm.

**Be-04.1.1 — Touch-only:** Pilot taps AP MODE control on the reused R01 panel to disengage; disengage requires a confirm (deliberate act, error-resistance folded in); panel reverts to manual/disengaged state on Screen.

**Be-04.1.2 — Keyboard-only:** Same via bezel OSS — press AP MODE OSS, confirm; disengaged state shown on Screen.

**Be-04.1.3 — Mixed:** Initiate on one modality, confirm on the other; disengaged state persists across both (mirrors R03 state-persistence).

One difference worth flagging vs. R03: disengagement is the safety-critical direction. On engage, an accidental press is annoying; on disengage, an accidental press drops automation unexpectedly. So the confirm step matters more here, not less — but it's the same mechanism, no new behaviour.

State-of-result feedback reuses R02's alert channel rather than a fresh cue.

**Closing Behaviour: Be-04.1.3 — dual-input (Touch/bezel) press-and-confirm disengage, state persisting across modalities, result confirmed via reused R02 channel.**

Moving to Structure.
Structure should pretty much be the same, just different texts.

Correct — same elements as R03, relabeled for disengage.

**S-04.1.3.1 — Reuse R03 AP MODE control on R01 panel.**
- R01-reused multi-input panel (WAD).
- Same AP MODE control (WAD touch target + mapped bezel OSS) — now toggles engaged→disengaged; press-and-confirm.
- Disengaged/manual state rendered on the panel (Screen), persisting across modalities.
- Result feedback via reused R02 channel (notification strip + panel cue + audio ping).

No new structure. The only deltas are label/state text ("AP MODE — DISENGAGE" / manual state) and the confirm prompt wording.

**Closing Structure: S-04.1.3.1 — R03 AP MODE control reused on R01 panel, relabeled for disengage, result confirmed via reused R02 channel.**

R04 complete:
- **F-04.1** — Relinquish automation authority to the pilot.
- **Be-04.1.3** — dual-input press-and-confirm disengage, state persisting across modalities.
- **S-04.1.3.1** — reused R03 AP MODE control (relabeled) + R01 panel + R02 feedback channel.

Ready to close R04, or anything to adjust?
